strengths: Novel integration of clustering, reasoning traces, function vectors, and meta-clustering to identify algorithmic primitives; the framework is intuitive and multi-faceted
Clear empirical validation: Table 1 convincingly shows primitive vectors reliably induce intended behaviors (e.g., nearest_neighbor +56.1% NN paths, compare_verify +655% verifications)
Comprehensive cross-task and cross-model analysis revealing meaningful differences between Phi-4 and Phi-4-Reasoning (e.g., verification primitives more common in reasoning variant)
Well-designed experiments with diverse reasoning tasks (TSP, 3-SAT, AIME, GraphNav), multiple models, and six behavioral measures supporting claims
Clear presentation with precise definitions, effective figures, and extensive appendices; paper is well-written and easy to follow
Demonstrates primitive transfer across tasks and compositional arithmetic effects, supporting the geometric organization hypothesis for some cases
weaknesses: Critical design choices lack justification and ablation studies: layer 17 (why not 10, 15, 20, 30?), k=50 clusters (sensitivity?), k=35 heads, minimum 4 meta-clusters. Results heavily dependent on arbitrary choices

Manual interpretation step (Step 2: mapping clusters to reasoning traces) introduces unquantified human bias; no inter-rater reliability reported, no systematic protocol documented, and only 5 responses per task for clustering—very small sample

Overstated universality claims: Abstract/intro claim 'universal primitives' and 'compositional generalization' but results show mostly task-specific primitives (Fig. 4 dissimilarity varies by task). Linear composition effects 'attenuated in Phi-4' (Fig. 5a)—hypothesis only weakly supported

Vector injection into residual streams does not prove causality; primitives likely correlate with but don't causally suffice/necessitate behavioral changes. Terminology 'causal patching' is imprecise; no comparison to true causal methods (gradient-based interventions, ablation of natural vectors)

Insufficient statistical rigor: no significance testing, confidence intervals, multiple comparisons correction, or error estimates. Claims of 'strong trend' (Figs. 9-10) lack quantitative support. Sample sizes (~100 examples, 5 for clustering) too small for generalization

Limited practical impact: paper is descriptive (what primitives exist), not prescriptive (how to improve reasoning). No demonstration that primitive knowledge enables better finetuning, more robust generalization, or novel capabilities

Compositional hypothesis inadequately validated: linear composition works for Llama-3-8B but fails for Phi-4 variants. Equation v_ℓ^(p⊕q) ≈ w_p v_ℓ^(p) ± w_q v_ℓ^(q) oversimplifies; conditions for validity unexplored. Non-linear interactions not examined

Reproducibility concerns: Phi-4/Phi-4-Reasoning proprietary and limited access, manual interpretation non-reproducible without original HTML interface, no code/checkpoints provided despite LLM usage disclosure

Cluster quality unvalidated: no internal cohesion metrics (silhouette, Davies-Bouldin), no external validation against held-out traces, k-means arbitrary without comparison to alternatives. Fig. 3b t-SNE only visual inspection

Task scope limitations: four tasks mostly discrete optimization/math; findings may not generalize to open-ended reasoning, retrieval, or diverse NLU. AIME diversity noted but not systematically explored

Cross-task transfer shown only on trivial operations (first/last node extraction); transfer from AIME to TSP described vaguely ('more paths, higher NN proportion') without quantitative validation. No ablation ruling out chance transfer
Nearest-neighbor analysis (Appendix E) reveals expected behavior (models use heuristics); minimal novelty. Claims like 'strong trend' (Fig. 9b) lack error bars and statistical tests

strengths: Comprehensive empirical study spanning four reasoning tasks and three models with systematic analysis of algorithmic primitives across multiple validation angles
Clear presentation of methodology with helpful visual illustrations (Figure 1, 3) and honest limitations discussion acknowledging when primitives don't map to known algorithms
Substantive findings comparing Phi-4 and Phi-4-Reasoning, revealing systematic differences in verification and path-generation primitive usage (Figure 4)
Reasonable framework combining clustering, manual interpretation, and function vectors, with multiple lines of validation including behavioral injection experiments
weaknesses: Critical methodological choices lack justification: k=50 clusters, layer 17, minimum 4 meta-clusters, and k=35 top attention heads are set without ablations or sensitivity analyses
Manual cluster interpretation from only 5 responses per task with no inter-rater agreement metrics, reproducibility documentation, or independent validation of the annotation process
Severe sample size limitations (n=5 initially, 100+ total mentioned but never specified precisely) without error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing throughout
Compositionality claims unsupported: linear composition assumption (v^(p⊕q) ≈ w_p v^(p) ± w_q v^(q)) fails in Phi models but this critical inconsistency is not adequately investigated
Cross-task transfer effects shown in Figures 2d and 5 are modest and lack statistical significance testing; compositionality achieves few-shot parity only in Llama-3-8B (Figure 8)

Overclaimed abstract results: 'universal primitives' claimed despite most being task-specific; 'compositional generalization after finetuning' shown only for specific primitives with inconsistent cross-model results
Limited novelty: function vector extraction methodology largely follows Todd et al. (2024); the main contribution is combining it with standard k-means clustering and manual interpretation

Behavioral hallmarks validation is weak: Table 1 shows contradictory effects (e.g., compare_verify injection increases verifications 655% but decreases final answer 7%); metrics rely on brittle string matching (Appendix D)
No ablation studies, no comparison to alternative interpretability methods, no human evaluation of whether identified primitives are meaningful
Reproducibility concerns: annotation guidelines not documented, generation parameters not fully specified, multiple hyperparameters fixed without justification, code availability not mentioned

strengths: Comprehensive, systematic framework combining clustering, reasoning trace alignment, function vectors, and compositional validation—well-motivated and clearly presented

Convincing validation experiments demonstrating that injected primitive vectors induce predicted behavioral hallmarks (Table 1: nearest_neighbor injection increases NN paths by 56.1%; subtraction shows reversal effects)
Novel finding of compositional primitives: adding TNR and RC vectors recovers few-shot performance in zero-shot on Llama-3-8B, suggesting genuine algebraic structure in primitive space
Mechanistic insights into Phi-4-Reasoning: demonstrates that reasoning finetuning increases verification and planning primitives, with causal evidence via injection
Cross-task transfer evidence: AIME primitives (spatial_reasoning, plan_final_answer) affect TSP performance, indicating some algorithmic generalization beyond memorization
Honest and thorough limitations discussion addressing reasoning vs. memorization and acknowledging constraints on linear composition and task scope
Good reproducibility: provides model names, layer selections, hyperparameters, task prompts, and systematic methodology that should be replicable
weaknesses: Critical subjectivity in primitive identification: clusters are labeled by manual inspection of associated tokens (Appendix A shows interpretive decisions like Cluster 35 being labeled for inductive vs. representational role). No inter-rater agreement reported, undermining reproducibility of the most important step

Limited evidence for universality claims: primitives are often task-specific (e.g., 'brute_force' specific to Phi-4's approach); TSP and AIME primitives within Phi-4-Reasoning differ substantially (Fig. 4e); cross-model transfer is weak (Llama-3-8B shows attenuated compositional effects, Section 5)

Experiments demonstrate sufficiency (injection induces behavior) but not necessity (models may not rely on these specific primitives); no ablations testing contradictory primitive injection or alternative representation directions

Unresolved reasoning vs. memorization: models may use 'amortized reasoning' from training examples rather than learned algorithms (acknowledged in Section 6, weakening claims about discovering true primitives)

Arbitrary hyperparameter choices without sensitivity analysis: k=50 clusters, layer 17 extraction, 'minimum four meta-clusters,' 35 heads (Phi-4) vs. 20 heads (Llama) lack justification or ablation studies

Artificial injection setups undermine some validity: Fig. 2b,c only generate 500 tokens (insufficient for task completion); behavioral hallmarks are indirect (counting words vs. measuring operations); Fig. 2c adds synthetic random paths

Limited scope: only four relatively structured reasoning tasks on transformer models of moderate size; unclear generalization to open-ended reasoning, other architectures, or contemporary larger models

Incomplete analysis of claims: 'compositional geometry' mentioned but mostly linear operations are validated; layer-dependence of injection effects not thoroughly analyzed; no direct evaluation of whether extracted primitives predict task performance
Paper is dense with many experiments; difficult to distinguish primary from supporting contributions; key results on graph operations and nearest-neighbor strategy relegated to appendix (Figs. 7-10)

strengths: Novel framework linking algorithmic primitives, compositional geometry, and neural representations with good neuroscience grounding
Comprehensive experimental design spanning multiple tasks (TSP, 3-SAT, AIME, GraphNav), models (Phi-4, Phi-4-Reasoning, Llama-3-8B), and analysis levels (behavioral, representational, causal)
Strong causal evidence via primitive vector injection with proper controls (bag-of-tokens baseline) demonstrating that primitives encode meaningful computations beyond token frequencies
Insightful mechanistic comparison between base and reasoning-finetuned models revealing systematic increases in verification and path-generation primitives after finetuning
Practical contributions including scalable automated LLM annotation pipeline (high agreement with manual labels), novel cluster expressivity metric, and cross-task transfer demonstration
Extensive supplementary evaluation with thorough ablations and robustness checks (hyperparameters, clustering choices, sample sizes)
Cross-task and compositional transfer results suggesting generalization of discovered primitives across domains
weaknesses: Conceptual looseness: 'algorithmic primitive' defined circularly through clustering then post-hoc validation; acknowledged limitation that primitives don't always map to known algorithms; ~17% of identified clusters are linguistic (punctuation, identifiers) rather than algorithmic

Methodological concerns with identification: layer 17 choice justified post-hoc with alternative layers (10-25) showing >0.95 correlation; k=50 motivated by elbow method but k=30, 50, 100 show >0.98 similarity; averaging top-35 attention heads uses Todd et al. (2024) designed for simple ICL, unclear if optimal for reasoning

Compositionality claims inadequately supported: addition of primitive vectors works for Llama-3-8B but fails for Phi-4/Phi-4-Reasoning (contradicting universality); only linear composition tested; sequential meta-cluster structure may reflect output ordering, not compositional geometry

Ambiguous evidence for algorithmic reasoning vs. memorization: unresolved tension between claims of learned algorithms and acknowledged possibility of amortized reasoning based on training data; limited analysis of whether primitives are true algorithms or training artifacts

Limited generalization: results dominated by Phi-4 family (proprietary models) with only Llama-3-8B as external baseline; scope limited to mathematical reasoning; 100+ examples per task is modest; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals

Evaluation metrics ad-hoc and task-specific: behavioral hallmarks (% NN paths, earliest token distance, word counting) lack principled justification; no cross-validation of whether primitive effects generalize to held-out problems

Limited mechanistic insight: identified primitives are behavioral categories, not circuits; no analysis of how primitives compose at attention/MLP level; Fig. 2b trajectories don't clearly show compositional structure
Model-specific failure of compositionality unexplained: why does TNR+RC addition work for Llama but not Phi models? Suggests findings may not be universal
Automated annotation only validates agreement with human labels, not ground truth about algorithmic meaning; potential circularity as LLM labels reflect training biases about reasoning
High computational cost (5-10 min per response on 4 A40 GPUs) and missing code availability limit reproducibility

strengths: Comprehensive multi-method framework connecting representations to behavior through clustering, annotation, and causal injection experiments
Important research question about compositional algorithmic structure in LLM reasoning
Extensive empirical evaluation across four reasoning tasks, three models, with thorough robustness checks in appendices
Causal intervention methodology using residual stream injection goes beyond typical representational analysis
Interesting empirical findings about differences between Phi-4 and Phi-4-Reasoning in verification and path-generation strategies
Well-organized presentation with clear visualizations and detailed supplementary material
weaknesses: Core claim about 'algorithmic primitives' is weakly justified—clusters are post-hoc labeled based on token co-occurrence, not demonstrated to represent causally relevant computational operations. Many identified clusters are explicitly linguistic rather than algorithmic

Causal claims are overstated: showing injected vectors can modulate behavior does not demonstrate these are the algorithmic primitives the model uses internally. Layer-dependent injection effects (Table 2) suggest layer-specific encodings rather than general primitives

Compositional geometry claims lack support: arithmetic composition of primitives fails for Phi-4/Phi-4-Reasoning (Fig. 10), and meta-clustering of transitions is merely descriptive, not evidence of compositional geometry

Insufficient engagement with reasoning vs. memorization: paper acknowledges models may use 'amortized reasoning' but doesn't demonstrate genuine compositional algorithmic generalization. Section 6 discussion is defensive rather than conclusive
Limited cross-task transfer evaluation—only TSP↔AIME tested in detail with modest effects. No systematic analysis of what transfers and why

Claims about 'compositional generalization after finetuning' (abstract) lack direct evidence. Differences in cluster frequencies (Fig. 4) don't prove models use different primitives or learn differently

Control experiments insufficient: only tests 'bag-of-tokens' alternative (Appendix F.1). Doesn't rule out that vectors encode task-relevant latent features exploitable post-hoc without revealing algorithmic structure
Layer choice (layer 17) affects identified primitives (Appendix G.1), suggesting findings may be somewhat artifact-dependent rather than discovering universal primitives
Limited methodological novelty—applies existing techniques (k-means clustering, function vectors from Todd et al., residual stream injection) to new domain rather than introducing new methods
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned, proprietary models (Phi-4, Phi-4-Reasoning), prohibitive computational cost (5-10 minutes per response on 4 A40 GPUs)

strengths: Well-motivated research question addressing whether LLM reasoning emerges from compositional geometric operations in activation space

Comprehensive multi-level methodology with principled design choices: clustering (layer 17, k=50), automated LLM annotation validated against manual labels, hierarchical meta-clustering, and function vector extraction with extensive ablations

Strong empirical validation: behavioral hallmarks show selective primitive induction (Table 2), controls for bag-of-tokens baseline (Table 5), layer/magnitude dependencies demonstrate specificity, and interference analysis reveals sequential structure

Novel insights on reasoning finetuning: systematic evidence that reasoning-finetuned Phi-4 uses more verification and structured reasoning primitives, suggesting algorithmic strengthening rather than memorization
Cross-task transfer demonstrated: primitives from AIME transfer to TSP, synthetic task primitives (TNR, RC) transfer to complex reasoning, with Fig. 5c showing predictable behavioral hallmarks

Excellent reproducibility and transparency: cluster expressivity metric, automated annotation pipeline with multiple prompting strategies, detailed hyperparameter justification (Appendix G), and robustness checks across layer/K/sample choices
weaknesses: Compositionality claims are overstated: linear composition (addition/subtraction) fails on Phi-4/Phi-4-Reasoning models while working on Llama-3-8B (Fig. 5a); most composition experiments are on simple synthetic tasks rather than complex reasoning tasks (TSP, AIME); non-linear interactions unexplored

Weak algorithmic grounding: paper doesn't verify primitives implement known algorithms; 8 of 46 clusters (17%) are 'linguistic' rather than 'algorithmic' (Table 3); authors acknowledge 'primitives do not always map to a known algorithm' (p. 9); no systematic verification that primitives explain task performance

Causality claims require stronger support: terminology uses 'causal patching' but mostly demonstrates behavioral association; lacks strong evidence through ablations, performance degradation from primitive removal, or necessity demonstrations; layer/magnitude dependencies suggest but don't prove causality

Cluster validation concerns: LLM annotation relies on GPT-4o interpretation; novel 'cluster expressivity' metric (unique tokens/radius) lacks validation against ground truth; no systematic evaluation of false positive rate; many clusters lack clear algorithmic meaning

Limited scope and generalization: only 3 models (Phi-4-Base, Phi-4-Reasoning, Llama-3-8B) and 4 specialized planning/search tasks; only 100+ examples per task (memorization plausible for TSP with 6-12 cities); reasoning vs. memorization discussion is superficial and not rigorously tested

Methodological choices appear post-hoc: layer 17 chosen despite layers 10-25 showing >0.95 correlation (Appendix G.1); k=50 despite k=30/50/100 giving nearly identical results (r>0.98); 35 attention heads from Todd et al. but not validated for reasoning primitives

No quantification of task performance impact: Table 2 measures behavioral hallmarks (e.g., '+656% verifications'), not actual task accuracy; unclear if primitive injections improve solution quality; cross-task transfer effects appear modest without significance testing

Limited technical novelty: clustering is standard; function vectors are from Todd et al. (2024); LLM annotation is straightforward application; contribution is primarily in application and interpretation rather than methodological innovation

Statistical rigor gaps: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing; effects measured on proxies rather than task performance; no baseline comparisons to alternative interpretability methods or simpler alternatives

Key findings relegated to appendices: nearest neighbor strategy analysis in Appendix D; some important experimental details scattered; 'primitive' terminology loose with heterogeneous meanings across contexts
